chunks: Muhammad ibn Ali Majilawayh (may Allah be pleased with him) narrated to us, saying: My uncle Muhammad ibn Abi al-Qasim narrated to me, from Muhammad ibn Ali al-Kufi, from Uthman ibn Isa, from Furat ibn Ahnaf, who said:

A man asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) and said: Those before us say: 'We seek refuge in Allah from the evil of Shaytan, the evil of the ruler, and the evil of the Nabatean if he is Arabized.' He said: Yes, shall I add to it for you? He said: Yes. He said: And from the evil of the Arab if he is Nabateaized. I said: And how is that? He said: The one who enters Islam and proclaims a master other than us has Arabized after his migration; this is the Nabatean when he is Arabized. As for the Arab when he is Nabateaized, it is the one who acknowledges the authority of the one because of whom he entered Islam and proclaims him instead of us; this one has been Nabateaized.

key_terms.النبطي: Nabatean (a non-Arab, often used to refer to Persians or non-Arabs in this context)
key_terms.الهجرة: Migration (referring to the migration to Islam or to the Ahl al-Bayt)
key_terms.الوالي: The master/authority (referring to the Ahl al-Bayt)

ai.seo_question: What is the meaning of the Arabization of the Nabatean and the Nabateaization of the Arab in Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In *Mani al-Akhbar*, Shaykh al-Saduq records this dialogue with Imam al-Sadiq (AS) to clarify the sociological and theological shift in early Islamic identity, where 'Arabization' signifies a non-Arab adopting the political allegiance of the Umayyad caliphate rather than the Ahl al-Bayt. Conversely, 'Nabateaization' describes an Arab who, despite his lineage, rejects the authority of the Imams and aligns with foreign or rival powers, effectively losing his spiritual distinctiveness. This hadith underscores the Shia emphasis on *Wilayah* as the true marker of faith, transcending mere ethnic or linguistic Arabization.
